## Subjective

68yo M, established patient with COPD GOLD 3 + 30 pack-year tobacco hx (quit 2018), presents with 4-day h/o progressive dyspnea + increased sputum (location: chest; quality: tightness, productive cough; severity: 7/10; duration: 4 days progressive; timing: worse at night; context: triggered by recent URI; modifying factors: home albuterol nebs partial relief). Sputum yellow-green, increased volume. Compliant with daily LABA/LAMA/ICS. PMH: COPD GOLD 3, HTN. FHx: father COPD. SHx: ex-smoker, no EtOH.

Resp: increased SOB. CV: denies chest pain. Constitutional: low-grade fever 99.8.

## Objective

VS: BP 138/82, HR 96, RR 22, T 99.8°F, SpO2 90% on RA (baseline 94%). Gen: in mild distress, can speak full sentences. HEENT: unremarkable. Cardiac: RRR. Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheezing, prolonged expiratory phase, no crackles. CXR ordered, reviewed in office: no acute infiltrate, hyperinflation consistent with COPD. Extremities: no edema. Neuro: A&O×3.

## Assessment

1. COPD exacerbation, moderate severity (J44.1) — likely viral trigger
2. Hypertension, controlled (I10)

## Plan

Outpatient management chosen given alertness, ability to speak in full sentences, SpO2 90%+. Started prednisone 40mg PO daily × 5 days. Increased albuterol nebs to q4h × 5 days, then taper. Continue maintenance LABA/LAMA/ICS. Patient counseled extensively on warning signs: SpO2 <88% on home pulse-ox, increased work of breathing, decision regarding hospitalization should symptoms not improve. F/u 48-72 hr by phone, in person 1 week. CXR was reviewed today, integrated with clinical presentation.
